site.name: forge-coder
site.summary: Forge Coder — agentic coding IDE (local demo) Fictional agentic coding product. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly. Page `index.html` — Agent run view Three-pane IDE-style layout: file tree (left) + agent chat (center) + live diff preview (right). Left — file tree: - Virtual TypeScript project (`atlas-cli`) with folder collapse, file-status badges (M for modified, + for newly added), and a summary footer. - Clicking any file marked M / + loads its diff into the right pane.

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full forge-coder system, prioritizing the primary chatbot/agent interface flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Forge Coder interface demonstrates a compelling 3-pane agentic IDE layout on desktop, but struggles significantly with responsiveness and completeness. Users on mobile face severe horizontal overflow that forces manual panning, while standard chat interactions like 'Enter to submit' are missing. Furthermore, a high proportion of primary controls and navigation tabs act as silent stubs, offering no feedback to users trying to explore the full feature set.

exploration_plan.goal: Thoroughly validate the agentic IDE interface, focusing on the three-pane interaction model (file tree, agent chat, live diff), chat functionality, and responsive behavior on mobile.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will systematically test the three main panes of the IDE layout. It will verify that file selection correctly loads diffs, agent chat messages can be submitted, and diff views can be toggled. Finally, it will run a mobile pass to assess how the dense three-pane layout adapts to smaller screens, paying special attention to the reported small tap targets.
assumptions: As a local fixture demo, top navigation links (Inbox, Runs, Settings) and external actions (Connect repo, VS Code) might be static stubs.
Clicking files in the left tree view dynamically updates the right diff view without full page reloads.
risk_hotspots: Mobile responsiveness and usability of the dense 3-pane layout
Small tap targets on navigation and toolbar buttons
State synchronization between file tree selection and diff preview pane
Handling of long chat histories and scrolling in the center pane

phases.title: Global Navigation and Toolbar
phases.objective: Verify global navigation links and primary actions.
key_checks: Click Inbox, Runs, Settings to check for navigation or modal popups.
Click 'Connect a repo' and 'Open in VS Code' to observe behavior (expecting alerts or stubs).
exit_criteria: All top-level navigation and utility buttons have been clicked and their responses recorded.

phases.title: File Tree and Diff Preview Integration
phases.objective: Test the interaction between the file tree (left) and the live diff preview (right).
key_checks: Click on a modified (M) or added (+) file in the tree (e.g., 'stream.ts' or 'chunker.ts').
Verify the diff pane on the right updates to show the selected file's contents.
Click 'Open editor' and 'Accept all changes' in the diff pane.
exit_criteria: Confirmed that clicking files updates the diff view and that diff viewing controls function.

phases.title: Agent Chat Interaction
phases.objective: Validate the central agent chat interface and input controls.
key_checks: Click '⏸ Interrupt' and '↻ Rerun' to check state changes in the run status.
Submit the form using the 'Send' button and observe the chat history update.
exit_criteria: Chat input form has been submitted and run control buttons have been interacted with.

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Stress Test
phases.objective: Evaluate the complex IDE layout on a constrained mobile viewport.
key_checks: Observe how the three panes (tree, chat, diff) are handled (e.g., stacked, tabbed, hidden).
Attempt to use the small tap target controls identified in the prescan (e.g., nav links, toggle buttons).
Submit a chat message on mobile.
exit_criteria: Mobile layout strategy is documented and critical interactions have been verified on the small screen.

coverage_targets.pages: Fully explore index.html (the only known page).
coverage_targets.features: Exercise file selection, diff toggling, chat submission, and run controls.
coverage_targets.mobile: Validate the layout transformation of the 3-pane IDE and assess tap target usability.

notes: Since elements like specific files in the tree weren't explicitly listed as individual interactables in the prescan summary (likely due to structural grouping), the agent will need to discover them during execution based on visual cues.

findings.user_goal: Interact with the IDE interface on a mobile device
findings.problem: The 3-pane layout is entirely unresponsive, forcing the page width to stretch to 757px on a 390px viewport.
findings.evidence: The layout warnings indicate 'Page width 757px exceeds viewport 390px', and panning horizontally reveals that the right and left panes do not stack vertically or collapse into a drawer.
findings.why_it_matters: Users accessing the tool from smaller screens are forced to constantly pan horizontally to read diffs or chat responses, making the tool essentially unusable on mobile.
findings.suggestion: Implement responsive breakpoints that stack the panes vertically, or hide the file tree and diff view behind toggleable side-drawers on screens narrower than 768px.

findings.user_goal: Submit a message to the agent quickly
findings.problem: Pressing the 'Enter' key inside the chat textarea inserts a newline but does not submit the form.
findings.evidence: Observed during exploration: 'Pressing the Enter key inside the chat textarea does not submit the message. The text remains in the input field.' Users are forced to explicitly tap 'Send'.
findings.why_it_matters: In modern chat and AI interfaces, users expect 'Enter' to submit the prompt (and 'Shift+Enter' for newlines). The lack of this pattern disrupts workflow speed and creates friction.
findings.suggestion: Add an event listener to the chat textarea that triggers form submission on the 'Enter' key, requiring 'Shift+Enter' for manual line breaks.

findings.user_goal: Navigate the app and use primary toolbar actions
findings.problem: A significant number of navigation links and primary buttons fail silently without providing any feedback.
findings.evidence: Actions on 'Inbox', 'Runs', 'Settings', 'Connect a repo', 'Open in VS Code', and 'Accept all changes' resulted in a '#' appended to the URL and no visual state change or alert.
findings.why_it_matters: Silent failures leave users wondering if the application is broken, if the action is loading invisibly in the background, or if the feature is simply unimplemented.
findings.suggestion: For prototype or upcoming features, apply a 'disabled' visual state or trigger a lightweight 'Coming soon' toast notification when the stubbed controls are clicked.
findings.source_hint: Global Nav Links and Right Pane Toolbar

findings.user_goal: Scroll through long agent outputs or diffs while keeping context
findings.problem: Vertical scrolling operates globally across the entire window, causing shorter panes (like the file tree) to scroll out of view entirely.
findings.evidence: Scrolling the main window revealed lower content in the chat but 'causes the shorter file tree (left pane) to scroll completely out of view, leaving empty space.'
findings.why_it_matters: In an IDE interface, users expect toolbars and file explorers to remain sticky or scroll independently so they don't lose access to navigation while reading long files.
findings.suggestion: Apply `overflow-y: auto` to the individual column containers (file tree, chat log, diff view) so they scroll independently, and lock the main body layout height to 100vh.

findings.user_goal: Toggle settings easily on touch devices
findings.problem: Several interactive elements possess critically small tap targets on mobile devices.
findings.evidence: The 'Auto-apply edits' checkbox is natively rendered at 13x13px. Global nav links and diff toggle buttons have heights around 32-37px.
findings.why_it_matters: Targets smaller than the recommended minimum of 44x44px lead to frustrating mis-taps, especially on complex or dense interfaces, disproportionately impacting users with motor difficulties.
findings.suggestion: Increase padding or use larger wrapper labels to expand the clickable footprint of these elements to at least 44x44px on mobile devices.

findings.user_goal: Read the chat input instructions on small screens
findings.problem: The chat textarea's fixed height causes placeholder text truncation on narrow screens.
findings.evidence: On the 390px viewport, the placeholder 'Reply, ask for a change, or request another pass…' wraps to a second line, but the fixed 38px height cuts the second line off vertically.
findings.why_it_matters: Truncated text makes the interface look unpolished and obscures instructional content from mobile users.
findings.suggestion: Allow the textarea height to automatically expand based on content wrapping, or rewrite the placeholder text to be concise enough to fit on one line for mobile viewports.

gaps: 62% of actions produced no visible URL/text change; this may indicate dead controls or repeated probes.
